entities.name: (unnamed) town of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Simple, unfenced town of low houses; clean and prosperous; folk in white wool or frieze.

refs.q: they came into the town of that folk, which was but simple, wholly unfenced for war, and the houses but low, and not great

entities.name: (unnamed) Mote-house of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: The great building that is the Innocent Folk's temple, assembly hall and guest-house.

refs.q: the door of the Temple, or Mote-house, or Guest-house, for it was all these

entities.name: Land of the Innocent Folk
entities.summary: Fair country of valleys and little hills east of the mountains, peopled by the Innocent Folk.

refs.q: the land was grown goodly, with fair valleys and little hills

spatial.travel_time_text: out of the mountains in three days from the Vale
spatial.note: beyond the mountains from the west

refs.q: in three days' time they were come out of the mountains, and in three more the said mountains were to behold but a cloud behind them

spatial.terrain_text: mountain ways, then fair valleys and little hills, then a wide peopled valley

refs.q: when they were gone eight days from the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts
On the evening of that day they came into the town of that folk
for oxen are but slow-going nags

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: No filth, famine, poverty or misery; merry, well-fed folk; the town has no war defences.

refs.q: Yet was there naught of filth or famine, nor any poverty or misery

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: They treat the seekers with reverence, as kings or gods.

refs.q: they set them down on a dais as though they had been kings, or rather gods
they passed by garths wherein the young corn was waxing, and vineyards on the hillsides

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: They have never seen horses; the elder saw one knight on horseback in his youth.

refs.q: the elder said that once in his young days he had led a man to the Well who was riding a horse and was clad in knightly array

facts.subject: Innocent Folk
facts.statement: Guests are bathed, robed in fine white wool, crowned with flowers and feasted with songs of earth's fairness.

refs.q: the words of the songs were simple and harmless, and concerning the fairness of the earth and the happy loves of the creatures

events.label: Welcome by the Innocent Folk
events.summary: The Innocent Folk receive Ralph and Ursula in their Mote-house as "Seekers after length of days".

refs.q: Welcome and thrice welcome to the Seekers after length of days

opportunities.idea: A peaceful, prosperous, unwalled people as a contrast culture (no war, no poverty).

ledger.summary: They leave with the Innocent Folk's messengers, who marvel at the horses (the elder once led a mounted knight to the Well in his youth). After three days they leave the mountains; in three more the mountains are only a cloud behind; then fair valleys and little hills without people. On the eighth day from the Vale they meet ruder shepherds with odd sheep, and on the ninth reach a wide, well-watered valley with cots, corn, cattle and vineyards. That evening they reach the Innocent Folk's town: simple, unwalled, low houses, no filth, famine or poverty, merry folk in white wool. At the Temple or Mote-house or Guest-house the elders hail them as "Seekers after length of days"; they are bathed, robed in white, crowned with flowers, seated on the dais like gods, feasted, and sung to.
ledger.geography_notes: From the Vale of Sweet Chestnuts: three days out of the mountains; three more until they are a cloud behind; fair valleys and little hills, unpeopled; on the eighth day, a green hillside with shepherds; on the ninth, a wide grassy, watered, partly wooded valley with cots, cornfields and hillside vineyards; then the town of the Innocent Folk (unwalled).
